# Supplementary Figure 4

## Getting the data

Processed data are deposited at ArrayExpress, genome assemblies at ENA:

| Data | Accession |
|---|---|
| Single-nucleus RNA-seq | `E-MTAB-17757` |
| Single-nucleus ATAC-seq | `E-MTAB-17776` |
| Genome assemblies | `PRJEB115767` |

Everything except the single-nucleus atlases is committed in this repository
under `data/reference/`: orthology maps, TF lists, SAMap scores, gene-to-GO
maps, TF activity, the differential expression tables and the SCENIC+ output.

Only the atlases need downloading. Put them in one folder and point
`DATA_DIR` at it; the files are used exactly as ArrayExpress delivers them, so
nothing needs renaming.

```
<DATA_DIR>/
`-- snRNA/
    `-- seurat/                                  E-MTAB-17757
        |-- BifurcaAtlas.rds
        |-- BrachiAtlas.rds
        |-- FormosaAtlas.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant.rds
        |-- GracilisAtlas_pregnant.rds
        |-- InfansAtlas.rds
        |-- PhallocerusAtlas.rds
        |-- PictaAtlas.rds
        |-- ProlificaAtlas.rds
        |-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant_juvenile.rds
        `-- TurneriAtlas_pregnant.rds
```

Panels use the combined atlas for *P. gracilis* and *P. turneri* unless stated
otherwise; Figure 1B uses the pregnant-only *P. turneri* atlas.

Every atlas carries a `cell_type` column, which the scripts use rather than
per-species cluster numbers.

## Panels in this file

| Panel | Chunk | Status |
|---|---|---|
| S4A | `sf4a` | dendrogram of 1 - SAMap score across the nine poeciliids |
| S4B | `sf4b` | bootstrapped tree from pseudobulk expression and GSI |

S4A re-plots the matrix behind Figure 2B as a tree; S4B asks the same question
from expression directly, so the two are independent checks of each other.

```{r knitr-setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = TRUE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.align = "center", dev = "png", dpi = 300)
```

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
## PURPOSE : Set the two paths every chunk below reads from, and load packages.
## PRODUCES: DATA_DIR, REF_DIR, SPECIES
## QUESTION: none - configuration only.

DATA_DIR <- "XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX"   # master folder described above
REF_DIR  <- "../../data/reference"            # reference tables, committed in this repo

stopifnot(dir.exists(DATA_DIR), dir.exists(REF_DIR))

## The atlases are read under the names ArrayExpress delivers, so nothing needs
## renaming after download.
ATLAS <- c(bifurca   = "BifurcaAtlas.rds",
           brachi    = "BrachiAtlas.rds",
           formosa   = "FormosaAtlas.rds",
           gracilis  = "GracilisAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant.rds",
           infans    = "InfansAtlas.rds",
           phallo    = "PhallocerusAtlas.rds",
           picta     = "PictaAtlas.rds",
           prolifica = "ProlificaAtlas.rds",
           turneri   = "TurneriAtlas_pregnant_non_pregnant_juvenile.rds")

ATLAS_PREGNANT <- c(gracilis = "GracilisAtlas_pregnant.rds",
                    turneri  = "TurneriAtlas_pregnant.rds")

atlas_path <- function(sp, pregnant = FALSE)
  file.path(DATA_DIR, "snRNA", "seurat",
            if (pregnant) ATLAS_PREGNANT[[sp]] else ATLAS[[sp]])


## Seurat is loaded first on purpose: its Bioconductor dependencies mask several
## dplyr verbs, so dplyr must come last to win
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(Seurat)
  library(dendextend); library(corrr); library(ape)
  library(tidyr); library(readr); library(tibble); library(stringr); library(dplyr)
})

## the species column in the orthology table is "brac_gene_name" for brachi
SPECIES  <- c("gracilis","bifurca","formosa","infans","phallo",
              "brachi","prolifica","picta","turneri")
ORTHO_COL <- setNames(paste0(c("gracilis","bifurca","formosa","infans","phallo",
                               "brac","prolifica","picta","turneri"), "_gene_name"),
                      SPECIES)
```

```{r sf4a, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
## PURPOSE : Supplementary 4A - cluster all retained clusters on 1 - Pearson
##           correlation of their SAMap profiles.
## PRODUCES: the dendrogram, printed in the document
## QUESTION: does the SAMap signal group cell types across species rather than
##           grouping all clusters of one species together?

mat <- as.matrix(read.csv(
  file.path(REF_DIR, "rna", "SAMap", "MappingValues_Pairwise_samap.txt"),
  row.names = 1))

samap_clusters <- c(
  "bi_0","bi_2","bi_3","bi_6","bi_7","bi_8","bi_12","bi_19",
  "pr_1","pr_3","pr_5","pr_6","pr_8","pr_9","pr_10","pr_12","pr_17",
  "tu_1","tu_2","tu_3","tu_4","tu_5","tu_9","tu_10","tu_11","tu_12",
  "fo_0","fo_1","fo_2","fo_5","fo_6","fo_7","fo_8","fo_9","fo_11",
  "pi_1","pi_2","pi_3","pi_4","pi_5","pi_6","pi_7",
  "in_0","in_2","in_3","in_4","in_5","in_6","in_7","in_12",
  "gr_0","gr_2","gr_3","gr_4","gr_5","gr_7","gr_10","gr_11","gr_14",
  "br_0","br_1","br_3","br_5","br_6","br_7","br_9","br_11","br_13","br_14")

## subset in the matrix's own order, as Diego's script does
keep      <- setdiff(rownames(mat)[rownames(mat) %in% samap_clusters],
                     grep("^ze_", rownames(mat), value = TRUE))
samap_mat <- mat[keep, keep]
diag(samap_mat) <- 1

## The matrix is labelled <two-letter species>_<cluster number>. The cleaned
## atlases no longer carry that clustering, so the cluster -> cell type key is
## committed alongside the matrix; see its `source` column for how each was set.
CLUSTER_KEY <- read.csv(file.path(REF_DIR, "rna", "SAMap", "cluster_cell_types.csv"))
cell_type_of <- setNames(CLUSTER_KEY$cell_type, CLUSTER_KEY$label)

## a species may have several clusters of one type, so the cluster id is kept in
## the label to keep rows distinguishable and traceable back to the matrix
pretty_label <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(cell_type_of[x]), x,
                                   sprintf("%s (%s)", cell_type_of[x], x))

rownames(samap_mat) <- colnames(samap_mat) <- pretty_label(rownames(samap_mat))

dend <- as.dendrogram(hclust(as.dist(1 - cor(t(samap_mat), method = "pearson")),
                             method = "average")) |>
  color_branches(k = 10) |>
  set("labels_cex", 0.5) |>
  set("labels_col", "black")

plot(dend, main = "1 - Pearson on SAMap profiles", horiz = TRUE)
```

### S4B - pseudobulk tree

```{r sf4b-orthologues}
## PURPOSE : Keep the strict 1:1 orthogroups present in all nine species, so the
##           pseudobulk profiles can be compared gene by gene.
## PRODUCES: ortho_clean - one row per orthogroup, one column per species
## QUESTION: none - this defines the shared gene space for the tree.

ortho <- read_csv(file.path(REF_DIR, "rna", "Orthology",
                            "orthology_table_orthofinder_possvm.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)

species_cols <- unname(ORTHO_COL)

is_single_copy <- function(x) !is.na(x) & !grepl(";", x)

ortho_clean <- ortho |>
  mutate(across(all_of(species_cols), ~ trimws(str_replace_all(., '"', '')))) |>
  filter(across(all_of(species_cols), is_single_copy)) |>
  ## drop the species prefix and the isoform suffix so ids match the atlases
  mutate(across(all_of(species_cols), ~ sub("^[a-z]+_", "", .))) |>
  mutate(across(all_of(species_cols), ~ sub("-T\\d+$", "", .)))

## a gene may only represent one orthogroup in any species
for (cl in species_cols) ortho_clean <- ortho_clean[!duplicated(ortho_clean[[cl]]), ]

nrow(ortho_clean)
```

```{r sf4b-pseudobulk}
## PURPOSE : Average expression per cell type in each species, then express every
##           gene relative to its own mean across cell types (GSI).
## PRODUCES: pseud_gsi - genes x (species_cell type), on the shared gene space
## QUESTION: none - this builds the matrix the tree is computed from.

## bifurca's gene ids are used as the common key across species
KEY <- ORTHO_COL[["bifurca"]]

pseudobulk_species <- function(sp) {
  obj <- readRDS(atlas_path(sp))
  m   <- as.matrix(AverageExpression(obj, group.by = "cell_type", layer = "counts")[[1]])

  ## drop mitochondrial and unannotated models, then strip the isoform suffix
  m <- m[!grepl("^(m-|nbis)", rownames(m)), , drop = FALSE]
  rownames(m) <- make.unique(sub("-.*$", "", rownames(m)), sep = "")
  m <- m[rowSums(m) > 0, , drop = FALSE]

  colnames(m) <- paste(sp, colnames(m), sep = "_")

  ## a two-column lookup with fixed names. Selecting c(KEY, ORTHO_COL[[sp]])
  ## instead would name the same column twice for bifurca, whose own column is
  ## the key, and inner_join rejects duplicated names in y.
  lut <- data.frame(sp_gene = ortho_clean[[ORTHO_COL[[sp]]]],
                    gene    = ortho_clean[[KEY]],
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  as.data.frame(m) |>
    tibble::rownames_to_column("sp_gene") |>
    inner_join(lut, by = "sp_gene") |>
    distinct(gene, .keep_all = TRUE)
}

tabs <- lapply(setNames(SPECIES, SPECIES), pseudobulk_species)

common <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(tabs, `[[`, "gene"))
message(length(common), " genes shared by all nine species")

pseud <- Reduce(function(a, b) inner_join(a, b, by = "gene"),
                ## dplyr:: is explicit because Seurat's Bioconductor dependencies
                ## export S4 generics of the same names that do not take data frames
                lapply(tabs, \(d) dplyr::filter(d, gene %in% common) |>
                                   dplyr::select(-sp_gene))) |>
  column_to_rownames("gene")

## GSI: each gene's profile relative to its own mean across cell types
pseud_gsi <- sweep(pseud, 1, rowMeans(pseud), "/")
dim(pseud_gsi)
```

```{r sf4b, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 8}
## PURPOSE : Supplementary 4B - build a cell-type tree from the placental species'
##           GSI profiles, with bootstrap support over resampled genes.
## PRODUCES: the tree with bootstrap-coloured nodes, printed in the document
## QUESTION: do homologous cell types group together with statistical support,
##           independently of the SAMap result?

## the tree is built on the placental species, as in the paper
PLACENTAL <- c("bifurca","turneri","prolifica","formosa","phallo")
dat <- pseud_gsi[, grepl(paste0("^(", paste(PLACENTAL, collapse = "|"), ")_"),
                         colnames(pseud_gsi))]

corr_method    <- "pearson"
bootstrap.reps <- 1000
set.seed(1)

## resample genes with replacement, rebuild the tree each time
## (approach from F. Murat, Kaessmann lab spermatogenesis paper)
mytrees <- lapply(seq_len(bootstrap.reps), function(i) {
  sampled <- dat[sample(nrow(dat), nrow(dat), replace = TRUE), ]
  cm <- sampled |> correlate(method = corr_method, diagonal = 1, quiet = TRUE) |>
    column_to_rownames("term")
  as.phylo(hclust(as.dist(1 - cm), method = "ward.D2"))
})

## show the topology that is most compatible with the whole set
parts <- prop.part(mytrees, check.labels = TRUE)
best  <- which.max(vapply(mytrees, \(t) sum(prop.clades(t, part = parts, rooted = FALSE),
                                            na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1)))
tree  <- mytrees[[best]]
boot  <- prop.clades(tree, part = parts, rooted = FALSE) / bootstrap.reps

node_col <- cut(boot, breaks = c(-Inf, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9, Inf),
                labels = c("red", "darkorange1", "darkgoldenrod1", "chartreuse3")) |>
  as.character()

plot(tree, cex = 1, edge.width = 2, label.offset = 0.01, no.margin = TRUE)
title(main = sprintf("1 - %s, %d genes, %d bootstrap replicates",
                     corr_method, nrow(dat), bootstrap.reps),
      cex.main = 1.1, line = -2)
nodelabels(pch = 21, col = "black", bg = node_col, cex = 2)
legend("right", legend = c("> 0.9", "> 0.7", "> 0.5", "< 0.5"),
       col = c("chartreuse3", "darkgoldenrod1", "darkorange1", "red"),
       pch = 19, title = "Bootstrap", inset = 0.05)
```
